entry.title: Connection while your baby is in intensive care
entry.summary: The authors describe ways of being present with a premature baby in an incubator, including talking or singing when the baby is awake and meeting their gaze. They keep the baby’s strength and response central to their examples of closer contact.
entry.cue: Your premature baby is in neonatal intensive care.
detail: Their account makes room for a familiar voice and eye contact even through the sides of an incubator. Connection is still part of the relationship when being together looks different.

They mention expressed milk when possible and forms of touch that attend to whether the baby is content or overwhelmed. Their example of holding the baby skin to skin comes only once the baby is strong enough.
This passage describes connection during intensive care; it gives no timetable for what a premature baby should manage.

references.locator: Awake voice, eye contact, milk where possible, strength and tolerance conditions

ageContext.readiness: For a premature baby in neonatal intensive care.
ageContext.note: The book gives no age deadline for this situation.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
